method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

sourceChecks.note: Health Canada primary guidance retrieved: skin pigmentation can affect oximeter accuracy and occult hypoxaemia; readings must be interpreted with signs/symptoms, not fixed race-based correction.
Primary Diabetes Canada foot guidance was retrieved in earlier review: inspect/protect injuries despite reduced sensation. This does not establish individualized triage timing.

items.assessment: Increasing support despite same saturation is important, but device brand is irrelevant filler and the keys are easy by only/unchanged phrasing.
issues: Increasing support despite same saturation is important, but device brand is irrelevant filler and the keys are easy by only/unchanged phrasing.

options: The increased requirement despite a similar saturation
That saturation is unchanged, so status is unchanged
The current saturation and target range, omitting the flow-rate change
The admission room-air saturation and original oxygen prescription
why: Stable saturation achieved with more support can conceal worsening function.
The oxygen requirement is part of the clinical trend.
The increase in support is necessary to interpret the apparently stable saturation.
The original values provide context but omit the current deterioration in support needs.

items.assessment: Clinical action is correct and supported by Health Canada; dismiss/indefinitely are excessive cues. Replace with plausible measurement-first delays.
issues: Clinical action is correct and supported by Health Canada; dismiss/indefinitely are excessive cues. Replace with plausible measurement-first delays.

options: Accept the displayed saturation and investigate anxiety as the main cause
Subtract a fixed percentage from every reading
Change the probe site and await the next routine observation before escalating
Assess the whole clinical picture and escalate the mismatch
why: An apparently acceptable reading does not exclude hypoxaemia or another serious cause of worsening dyspnoea.
No universal numerical correction is established for individuals.
Measurement verification is useful but must not delay assessment and escalation of worsening symptoms.
Device limitations can contribute to missed hypoxaemia.

items.assessment: SATA distractors contain only while key options are comprehensive. Narrow the stem to respiratory response and make alternatives comparable process/systemic measures.
issues: SATA distractors contain only while key options are comprehensive. Narrow the stem to respiratory response and make alternatives comparable process/systemic measures.

options: The time at which the latest antibiotic dose was given
Completion of the prescribed sputum specimen collection
Work of breathing and activity tolerance
Oxygen requirement and respiratory-rate trend
why: Dose timing measures treatment delivery rather than respiratory response.
Specimen collection supports diagnosis but does not show whether respiratory function improved.
These reflect functional respiratory response.
Support needs and rate help identify improvement or worsening.
proposedChanges.stem: Which observations most directly evaluate respiratory improvement during treatment of a respiratory infection? Select all that apply.

items.assessment: Cup preference and future appointment are filler among acute findings. Use parallel relevant findings.
issues: Cup preference and future appointment are filler among acute findings. Use parallel relevant findings.

options: Respiratory rate remaining at the documented baseline
Increasing drowsiness with poorer airway clearance
Small amounts of sputum becoming easier to expectorate
Mild incisional discomfort unchanged from baseline
why: A stable rate is less concerning than new drowsiness with impaired airway clearance.
Reduced alertness threatens ongoing airway protection.
Improved clearance is less urgent than a decline in alertness and cough effectiveness.
Stable discomfort is less urgent than declining airway protection.

items.assessment: Three only-options cue the comprehensive key. Use plausible single-domain summaries without artificial qualifiers.
issues: Three only-options cue the comprehensive key. Use plausible single-domain summaries without artificial qualifiers.

options: Intake and estimated losses with current observations
Stool frequency and the last bowel movement time
Reported thirst and the amount of water offered
Usual weight and pre-illness drinking habits
why: The combined pattern suggests clinically important volume depletion.
This describes part of the loss but misses its amount and the current perfusion response.
Offered water is not necessarily consumed or sufficient; integrate actual intake, losses and observations.
Baseline habits give context but do not characterize the current deficit.

items.assessment: Individualized action-plan thresholds avoid generic numeric rules; increased breathlessness and rapid excess weight are appropriate triggers. Inconsistent measurement needs correction but does not itself establish clinical worsening.
Stem asks what to assess while alternatives include assumption and preference. Use comparable physiological concerns.
issues: Stem asks what to assess while alternatives include assumption and preference. Use comparable physiological concerns.

options: Reduced renal production from fluid depletion
Urine concentration after reduced overnight drinking
Possible bladder retention
Increased urine loss from an unrecorded diuretic dose
why: Dehydration is possible, but normal intake with pressure and prostate enlargement makes retention the more direct concern.
Concentration does not explain lower abdominal pressure and very limited emptying.
Obstruction can reduce voided output without stopping urine production.
Diuretic-related excess output does not fit the described pressure with minimal voiding.

items.assessment: A new unilateral painful change cannot be attributed to chronic bilateral oedema; assessment and escalation are appropriate. Massage and routine weight review are inadequate. This overlaps risk066 and should be separated in practice sessions.
Acute declining consciousness needs immediate assessment, not communication alone. Add responsiveness/airway/breathing check and remove only-pain filler.
issues: Acute declining consciousness needs immediate assessment, not communication alone. Add responsiveness/airway/breathing check and remove only-pain filler.

options: Check responsiveness, airway and breathing while activating urgent review
Give the prescribed analgesic and repeat orientation after it takes effect
Wait for the next routine observation time
Assume tiredness because it is evening
why: Declining consciousness requires immediate patient assessment and urgent escalation with baseline comparison.
Analgesia does not address new impaired arousal and must not delay urgent assessment.
An acute change requires assessment sooner than routine timing.
Time of day does not safely explain a new decline.

items.assessment: Sudden unprecedented severe headache and associated neurological decline are appropriate urgent red flags; familiar responsive or mild gradual patterns lack those supplied red flags. Item does not claim the latter can never need assessment.
Clinical key is too generic for unusual unresponsiveness and oral fluids is an obvious dangerous distractor. Make immediate safety assessment explicit.
issues: Clinical key is too generic for unusual unresponsiveness and oral fluids is an obvious dangerous distractor. Make immediate safety assessment explicit.

options: Place the client in their usual sleep position and reassess at the next scheduled check
Wait for the next scheduled medication round
Assess airway, breathing and responsiveness and obtain urgent review
Assume all post-seizure sleep is expected
why: Atypical prolonged unresponsiveness requires immediate reassessment rather than assuming sleep.
Medication timing does not justify delaying evaluation.
A prolonged altered state differs from the known recovery pattern and may indicate an ongoing emergency.
The atypical duration needs reassessment.

items.assessment: Protecting a painless lesion and arranging foot assessment recognizes sensory-loss risk; continued pressure or independent blister opening are relevant misconceptions. Routine skin care does not replace lesion assessment.

Vomiting/no meal changes the prandial-insulin context. Current glucose and authorized individualized plan review are appropriate; the item avoids universal withholding of all insulin and avoids inventing a dose.
Two only distractors reveal SATA keys. Specify assessment of extent and injury-related risk, preserving real alternative observations.
issues: Two only distractors reveal SATA keys. Specify assessment of extent and injury-related risk, preserving real alternative observations.

options: Recent falls or other trauma
The colour changes in a single resolving bruise
Whether the anticoagulant was taken before or after breakfast
Bleeding from gums, urine, or stool
why: Injury history changes the assessment of occult bleeding risk.
A resolving local bruise does not assess the new pattern’s extent or injury exposure.
Meal timing does not directly assess the extent of bleeding or recent injury.
Other sites help assess the extent of bleeding.
proposedChanges.stem: A client taking an anticoagulant develops multiple unexplained bruises. Which additional findings most directly assess the extent of bleeding or injury-related bleeding risk? Select all that apply.

items.assessment: Expected ageing and weeks-long delay are cartoon alternatives. Use realistic causal misattribution while preserving acute-illness key.
issues: Expected ageing and weeks-long delay are cartoon alternatives. Use realistic causal misattribution while preserving acute-illness key.

options: Treat the reduced intake as the main cause and monitor after nutritional supplements
Use a routine cough suppressant and reassess at the next scheduled review
Assess for acute illness despite the normal temperature
Exclude infection because fever is absent
why: Poor intake may be a manifestation of acute illness; new cough and functional decline warrant assessment now.
Symptom suppression does not evaluate the associated acute functional deterioration.
Older adults may show infection through functional and cognitive changes.
No fever does not reliably rule out infection.

items.assessment: Report question options are only/all claims; use relevant alternative summaries.
issues: Report question options are only/all claims; use relevant alternative summaries.

options: The diabetes history and most recent glucose result
Position-linked symptoms and measured pressure changes
The pressure after seated recovery and the duration of rest
Recent antihypertensive timing and the usual baseline pressure
why: Glucose is relevant, but this omits the measured positional pressure response associated with symptoms.
These document orthostatic intolerance needing plan review.
Recovery information alone omits the symptomatic standing response.
These may help identify causes but should accompany the direct position-linked observations.

items.assessment: Snack preference is filler and repeated only cues the keys. Ask specifically for acute changes with parallel findings.
issues: Snack preference is filler and repeated only cues the keys. Ask specifically for acute changes with parallel findings.

options: The new change in mental status
The abdominal trend with weight and symptoms
Prominent abdominal veins unchanged from prior assessment
Usual mild ankle swelling without recent increase
why: This may reflect a serious complication requiring assessment.
Fluid accumulation and associated symptoms need evaluation.
This chronic stable observation is less urgent than the new neurological and fluid trends.
The unchanged baseline adds less urgency than new confusion and increasing abdominal girth.
proposedChanges.stem: A client with chronic liver disease has increasing abdominal girth and new confusion. Which findings indicate current deterioration that should be promptly communicated? Select all that apply.

items.assessment: Odour/appliance-order distractors are unrelated to acute dehydration. Use plausible self-management errors.
issues: Odour/appliance-order distractors are unrelated to acute dehydration. Use plausible self-management errors.

options: Reduce oral fluids to slow the intestinal output
Increase plain water and defer contacting the team until the next day
Change to a larger pouch and review output at the next routine visit
Assess hydration and promptly contact the team
why: Reducing intake may worsen dehydration and requires individualized team advice.
Symptomatic high losses need prompt assessment; fluid and electrolyte replacement should follow an individualized plan.
A larger appliance manages containment but does not address dizziness and low urine output.
High losses with perfusion symptoms suggest dehydration risk.

items.assessment: Larger meal is a weak filler distractor. Replace with a plausible comfort-first delay.
issues: Larger meal is a weak filler distractor. Replace with a plausible comfort-first delay.

options: Increase fibre as the immediate treatment
Give the prescribed antiemetic and reassess after the next bowel-care round
Assess and urgently seek clinical review
Administer the usual laxative before assessment
why: Fibre does not address a possible obstructed bowel.
Symptom relief must not delay urgent assessment of possible obstruction.
The pattern may indicate obstruction rather than routine constipation.
Stimulating the bowel may be inappropriate with suspected obstruction.

items.assessment: Interpretation question mixes action with diagnosis and uses permanent-ruleout caricature. Make parallel plausible interpretations.
issues: Interpretation question mixes action with diagnosis and uses permanent-ruleout caricature. Make parallel plausible interpretations.

options: The meal symptoms can be managed under the existing plan because the earlier screen was normal
A reassessment is needed despite the earlier screen
The weight loss is nutritional, since a swallowing problem would have been found on the screen
The coughing is unlikely to affect intake if it occurs only during some meals
why: A previous screen does not address later cough and weight loss.
A screen is time-specific and does not override subsequent concerns.
Screening is time-specific and may miss later or more complex swallowing problems.
Intermittent symptoms may still be clinically important and require reassessment.

items.assessment: Fluid weight can conceal tissue loss; poor intake and reduced muscle bulk justify comprehensive nutritional assessment despite stable scale weight. No single anthropometric measure substitutes for assessment.

Fatigue and increased assistance represent changed capacity requiring mobility-plan reassessment. Different preferred time alone and an unchanged aid do not establish functional decline. Preference should still inform planning.
Stopping all oxygen until discharge is implausible. Replace with relevant pressure workaround; key correctly overrides a global low-risk score.
issues: Stopping all oxygen until discharge is implausible. Replace with relevant pressure workaround; key correctly overrides a global low-risk score.

options: Repeat the score without inspecting the site
Add padding over the tender point before checking the skin or device fit
Assess the device contact area directly
Dismiss pressure risk because the score is low
why: Rescoring alone can miss the local problem.
Padding may not remove the pressure and may alter fit; inspect the contact area first.
A global score may not capture localized device pressure.
A score does not override a new clinical symptom.

items.assessment: Improved urine/postural symptoms and pulse/alertness are physiological responses. Intake balance or completed fluid bag are process measures; this is a useful evaluation distinction.
Cancel-followup and immediate discharge are too absolute. Use realistic premature-normalization alternatives.
issues: Cancel-followup and immediate discharge are too absolute. Use realistic premature-normalization alternatives.

options: Reassess and escalate the evolving symptoms
Repeat routine observations after a rest period because consciousness has returned
Attribute the palpitations to anxiety from the faint and provide reassurance
Focus only on the minor elbow bruise
why: Transient recovery does not explain or resolve the event's cause.
New palpitations after unexplained syncope require timely assessment, not routine deferred monitoring.
Anxiety is possible, but the evolving circulatory symptoms need assessment before attribution.
The evolving circulatory symptoms take priority over a minor injury.

overlapNotes: risk083 and066 test the same unilateral calf-change concern in different baseline contexts. Separate in practice sets; full-bank objective deduplication remains needed.
Multiple acute-change questions still share an assess/escalate response. Proposed changes improve distractors but do not establish high difficulty or psychometric discrimination.
